message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on Pacific Avenue in this Monopoly auction.

I have $919 and no monopolies. The auction is at $250 with only p2 and me still bidding. If p2 wins, they would control two greens against one from p4.

Bidding $251 leaves $668 cash. That covers both the Tennessee and Marvin denials. A $300 bid leaves $619, still enough for both denials but with a tighter buffer. A $350 bid would leave only $569 after denials, which is risky.

Blocking p2 from two greens is strategically valuable. p4 is cash-poor and vulnerable, so they might sell North Carolina later. If p2 then buys NC from them, they would own a full green monopoly. p2 already controls red and dark blue properties.

Pennsylvania Avenue is green, not red. The full color group breakdown shows p4 owns two light blues and two pinks, while p1 owns two reds and two oranges. p2 holds one orange and one yellow.

I will bid the minimum $251. Jumping higher would let p2 dictate near full price.

p2 has been escalating aggressively, so a $251 bid may not be enough to stop them. I am weighing the expected value of blocking p2 from a second green against the need to keep cash for the Tennessee denial. An orange monopoly would be devastating because St. James and New York are heavily landed on.

Marvin Gardens would not form a yellow monopoly by itself. Bidding $300 on Pacific leaves $619, which still covers the $180 Tennessee denial and leaves $439 remaining.

p2 has $613 in cash. After a $250 bid they would retain $363, so they can afford to escalate further. They may push the auction toward $350 or $400. A $350 bid on my side would leave only $109 after both denials, which is too tight.

A $251 bid is clearly positive expected value. It keeps the green split three-way and leaves a healthy buffer after both denials. I will stay incremental and avoid revealing a ceiling. The public message should be brief and slightly dismissive to avoid looking desperate.
